WARNING: SYNTHETIC CAPABILITY DEMONSTRATION. Not a result, not a benchmark, and not evidence about the hackathon dataset. The rings below were planted by this script and then found by this script. Its only purpose is to show that the Stage 6 code path executes when a counterparty ledger exists.
why_this_exists: reports/04_graph_report.json records that the real dataset has no counterparty column, so Stage 6 disables itself. This demonstrates the disabled code.
how_this_score_is_consumed: As a 0.15 blend weight on the calibrated probability in 05_score_explain.py, never as a standalone alert. The per-hop breakdown matters because reach and noise diverge sharply with distance, and a single 'flagged / not flagged' number hides that.
interpretation: Stopping after one hop puts 93 accounts in the queue and recovers 33 of 36 unknown ring members, at 35% precision. Letting it run to hop 3 reaches 100% recall but inflates the queue to 1222 accounts at 3% precision, roughly 33.9 alerts for every member found. That collapse is the honest argument against untuned propagation: on a graph with ordinary background traffic, three hops reaches most of the bank. It is also why the pipeline consumes this as a 0.15 blend weight rather than as an alert, and why a deployment would cap it at one or two hops and tune the decay against its own transaction density.
